description: A single-panel figure consisting of one rendered table (no axes, curves, spectra or micrographs) that sets the theoretical thermodynamic criteria for regular solid-solution formation in high-entropy alloys against the calculated parameters of the non-equiatomic FeMnNiAlSiC high-entropy steel studied in this work. Seven columns are headed: Thermodynamic parameter, ΔH_mix (kJ/mol), ΔS_conf (J/K-mol), δ (%), Ω (Dimensionless), VEC (Dimensionless) and References. The first data row, 'Regular solid solution', gives the reference windows −22 ≤ ΔH_mix ≤ 7, 11 ≤ ΔS_conf ≤ 19.5, δ ≤ 6.6, Ω ≥ 1.1, and three stacked VEC criteria — VEC ≥8.0 FCC, VEC <6.87 BCC, 6.87 < VEC <8.0 BCC + FCC — cited to [42,43]. The second row, 'Present work' (This work), gives ΔH_mix = −8.4, ΔS_conf = 12.4, δ = 7.6, Ω = 2.4 and VEC = 6.9. Reading the two rows together, the alloy satisfies the ΔH_mix, ΔS_conf and Ω criteria, and VEC = 6.9 places it inside the 6.87 < VEC < 8.0 BCC + FCC band, but its δ = 7.6 % exceeds the δ ≤ 6.6 % limit. The table supports the argument that this composition forms a (modestly distorted) solid solution with mixed BCC + FCC character. No other values are printed.

observations.observation: The figure is a single rendered table with seven columns: Thermodynamic parameter, ΔH_mix (kJ/mol), ΔS_conf (J/K-mol), δ (%), Ω (Dimensionless), VEC (Dimensionless) and References.
The 'Regular solid solution' row gives the theoretical window −22 ≤ ΔH_mix ≤ 7 kJ/mol and 11 ≤ ΔS_conf ≤ 19.5 J/K-mol.
The 'Regular solid solution' row gives δ ≤ 6.6 % and Ω ≥ 1.1 as the criteria for regular solid-solution formation.
Three VEC criteria are printed in the 'Regular solid solution' row: VEC ≥8.0 for FCC, VEC <6.87 for BCC, and 6.87 < VEC <8.0 for BCC + FCC.
The 'Present work' row prints ΔH_mix = −8.4 kJ/mol, ΔS_conf = 12.4 J/K-mol, δ = 7.6 %, Ω = 2.4 and VEC = 6.9.
For the present alloy ΔH_mix = −8.4 kJ/mol lies inside the −22 ≤ ΔH_mix ≤ 7 window, and ΔS_conf = 12.4 J/K-mol lies inside 11 ≤ ΔS_conf ≤ 19.5, so both enthalpy and entropy criteria are satisfied.
Ω = 2.4 for the present work satisfies the Ω ≥ 1.1 criterion shown in the criteria row.
δ = 7.6 % for the present work exceeds the tabulated δ ≤ 6.6 % limit, i.e. the alloy does not meet the size-mismatch criterion.
VEC = 6.9 for the present work falls inside the tabulated 6.87 < VEC < 8.0 band, which the table assigns to a BCC + FCC phase mixture.
The criteria row is attributed to references [42,43], while the present-work row is attributed to 'This work'.

The caption states that the table presents the theoretical criteria of the thermodynamic parameter for regular solid-solution formation in HEAs together with the thermodynamic parameters of the non-equiatomic FeMnNiAlSiC HES.
The table contains no sample label for the present alloy beyond 'Present work'; the specific composition (FeMnNiAlSiC) comes from the caption and paper title, not from the table itself.

subfigures.description: One rendered table with seven columns (Thermodynamic parameter, ΔH_mix (kJ/mol), ΔS_conf (J/K-mol), δ (%), Ω (Dimensionless), VEC (Dimensionless), References) and two data rows: 'Regular solid solution' (theoretical criteria, refs [42,43]) and 'Present work' (This work).
